_doc: Per-example reading overrides for the audio workflow (AUDIO_WORKFLOW.md §3.2). An override replaces the example's text, for recording and checking only, with `say`: the same sentence with a reading spelled out in kana where the furigana cannot express it (a quoted particle は said wa). `h` is the short text hash of the example the override was written for: when the example is edited, the override stops applying and the example is held back (reason override-stale) until the override is updated or removed. A recording older than `added` is re-recorded.

03351_joshi_ex1.say: 「わ」と「が」は{日本語|にほんご}の{代表|だいひょう}{的|てき}な{助詞|じょし}だ。
03351_joshi_ex1.why: 「は」 names the particle, pronounced wa; the furigana cannot say so (MeCab tags a lone quoted は as a symbol, so it would be read ha).

20890_fukujoshi_ex1.say: 「わ」は{副助詞|ふくじょし}に{分類|ぶんるい}される。
20890_fukujoshi_ex1.why: 「は」 names the particle, pronounced wa; the furigana cannot say so (MeCab tags a lone quoted は as a symbol, so it would be read ha).

29609_kakarijoshi_ex1.say: 「ワ」や「モ」は{係助詞|かかりじょし}だ。
29609_kakarijoshi_ex1.why: 「は」 names the particle, pronounced wa; the furigana cannot say so (MeCab tags a lone quoted は as a symbol, so it would be read ha). Katakana here: with hiragana 「わ」や the TTS said わいや on all five attempts.
